1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: That you take, that you adopt — a present-tense verb (form VIII) meaning to take for oneself, to choose or adopt something. Addressed to a group ('you all'), and in a form used after particles meaning 'that' or 'to'.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb in the reflexive (form VIII) pattern, 'to take for oneself'. The ta- prefix with the plural ending means 'you all'. The ending is -ū (the final 'n' of -ūna has dropped), which marks the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form used after particles like 'that', 'to', or 'not'.

6.meaning: "My enemy" — an adversary, one who is hostile; the singular form is often used collectively for a whole hostile group, so it can carry the sense "my enemies."
6.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -ī, "my." The final -ī swallows the case vowel, so the word simply reads "my enemy"; ʿaduww is an intensive pattern meaning one persistent in hostility, and Arabic often uses it as a collective for many enemies.

7.meaning: 'And your enemy / your foe'. The base word means an adversary or opponent; with the attached 'your', it names the enemy belonging to or opposed to a group of people.
7.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -kum ('your', for a group of you, masculine plural) marking possession. The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative ending, typically marking the noun as a direct object or otherwise governed in the accusative.

8.meaning: Allies, protectors, intimate friends — those taken as close supporters, patrons, or guardians, with whom one stands in mutual loyalty (plural of walī).
8.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'walī.' Being a 'diptote' (a noun that resists the usual full set of endings), it takes a single final '-a' here for the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb or signals 'as / being' something — and notably without the usual '-n' (no nunation).

9.meaning: "You (all) cast / extend / offer" — to throw something toward someone; used figuratively of extending affection or secretly conveying messages.

parts.en: cast, offer (stem of alqā, "to throw toward")

9.grammar: Present-tense (imperfect) verb, Form IV (causative: "make something reach, cast toward"). The tu- prefix marks "you," and the -ūna ending marks the masculine plural "you all" in the normal (indicative) mood — an ongoing or habitual action.

10.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
10.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
10.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

11.meaning: "With affection/love" — mawadda is warm, expressed love and friendship: affection that shows itself in loyalty and closeness, stronger and more demonstrative than mere liking.
11.grammar: The preposition bi- ("with") is attached to the noun, and prepositions always put their noun in the genitive case — that is what the final -i marks. The tā' (-t-) is the feminine noun ending.

12.meaning: 'And indeed / while already' — the word 'wa' ('and, while') joined to 'qad', a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
12.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and', or circumstantial 'while') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' emphasizes completion and certainty ('has indeed already…'); with a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes' or 'may'.

13.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
13.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

14.meaning: A compound meaning roughly 'because of what...', 'on account of that which...', or 'by means of what...'. It joins the preposition 'with/by/because of' to a connector 'what/that which', introducing the reason or instrument for something.
14.grammar: A preposition (bi-) fused to the word mā ('what / that which'). The preposition bi- expresses cause, means, or accompaniment; combined with mā it forms a phrase pointing to the thing or fact that serves as a reason or means ('because of what...').

15.meaning: "he/it came to you" — a past verb "came" with the pronoun "you" as the one reached, i.e. something arrived at or reached a group of people.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb in its base third-person masculine singular form ("he/it came"), with no extra subject suffix. The verb "to come" is intransitive, so the attached -kum is not a direct object but an indirect (dative) pronoun — "to you" (masculine plural), equivalent to "came to you (all)."

16.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
16.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

17.meaning: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
17.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
17.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

18.meaning: "They drive out / expel" — to force someone to leave, to make them go out from their home or land.

parts.en: drive out, expel (stem of akhraja, causative of "go out")

18.grammar: Present-tense verb, Form IV — the causative pattern: kharaja means "to go out," so akhraja means "to make someone go out," i.e. expel. The yu- prefix marks "they," and -ūna marks the masculine plural in the normal (indicative) mood.

19.meaning: The messenger, envoy, or emissary: one who is sent with a message; in the Qur'an typically a prophet sent by Allah bearing revelation to a people.
19.grammar: A noun on the form faʿūl (an intensive/agent pattern, 'one sent'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -a ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb ('… the messenger') or the subject of certain particles. The 'l' of al- assimilates into the following 'r' (a 'sun letter'), pronounced ar-rasūl.

20.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and you (plural)' used as a standalone object — 'and you yourselves.' The base iyyā- is a special particle that carries an object pronoun when it cannot attach directly to a verb, here with 'you all.'
20.grammar: A connective 'and' joined to a detached object pronoun. The element iyyā- exists precisely to bear an object pronoun in isolation (when it cannot be suffixed onto a verb); the attached -kum means 'you all' (masculine plural) and functions as the object.

21.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
21.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

22.meaning: You (plural) believe — to have faith, to trust and affirm as true, especially trust in Allah and what He has revealed; also to be secure or to grant security.
22.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the form meaning 'to have faith'. The 'tu-' prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the shortened '-ū' ending (without final 'na') indicates the subjunctive/jussive mood — the form used after certain particles such as 'that', 'in order to', 'if', or negation.

23.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
23.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
23.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

24.meaning: 'Your Lord' — Rabb denotes the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, possesses, and brings each thing to its completion; joined to 'your' (plural).
24.grammar: A noun 'Lord' in the genitive case (the -i ending), which typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The suffix -kum is the possessive 'your' addressed to a group.
24.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship: nurturing, mastering, owning, sustaining

25.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
25.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

26.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
26.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. As the doer is built into the suffix, the verb itself is in its base past form ('you all were').
26.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

27.meaning: "You (all) went out / came forth" — to leave, set out, emigrate from a place.
27.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb. The suffix -tum is the subject marker meaning "you all (masculine plural)" — the past tense in Arabic shows its subject by such endings rather than by prefixes.

28.meaning: Jihād — "striving, exertion of utmost effort": the verbal noun of struggling with all one's resources in Allah's cause; broader than fighting, it covers every earnest struggle for His sake.
28.grammar: A verbal noun (the act of striving). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative: it commonly marks the object of a verb or an adverbial sense such as "striving" / "in order to strive."

29.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
29.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

30.meaning: My way, path, or road — and by extension a course of conduct or a cause one travels toward; with the attached 'my' it denotes the path belonging to the speaker.
30.grammar: A masculine noun carrying the first-person singular possessive ending -ī ('my'). When that pronoun is attached, it both claims ownership and stands in the place where a case-vowel would otherwise show.

31.meaning: And the seeking, desiring, or pursuit of something: actively striving after a goal. A verbal noun denoting the act of looking for and wanting.
31.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a verbal noun of the eighth form, naming the act of seeking. The final -a ending is accusative, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb or to express purpose ('out of / seeking'); it can also follow certain particles.
31.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after

32.meaning: "My good pleasure" — marḍāt is the state of being pleased and approving; with "My" it means seeking Allah's approval and acceptance.
32.grammar: A noun of the maf'ala pattern (naming the state of being pleased) with the attached pronoun -ī, "my." The -ī absorbs the case vowel, so the form is simply "My pleasure"; the -ti before it is the feminine tā' of the noun.

33.meaning: You keep secret / conceal — to hide something within, to keep it private or undisclosed. Asarra means to do or hold something inwardly, the opposite of making it public.
33.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in Form IV (the causative pattern). The tu- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ūna suffix makes it masculine plural ('you all') in the indicative mood, signalling an ongoing or habitual action.
33.root: س-ر-ر (s-r-r) — secret, that which is hidden within

34.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
34.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
34.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

35.meaning: "With affection/love" — mawadda is warm, expressed love and friendship: affection that shows itself in loyalty and closeness, stronger and more demonstrative than mere liking.
35.grammar: The preposition bi- ("with") is attached to the noun, and prepositions always put their noun in the genitive case — that is what the final -i marks. The tā' (-t-) is the feminine noun ending.

36.meaning: And I — the standalone first-person singular pronoun 'I,' here joined by 'and.' As a detached pronoun it stands on its own (typically as subject), unlike the attached endings.
36.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and.' 'anā' is the independent (detached) pronoun 'I,' used for emphasis or to begin/identify the subject; it does not take a case ending and is fixed in form.

37.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
37.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.

38.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
38.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

39.meaning: "You (all) concealed / kept hidden" — to hide something so it is not seen or known.

parts.en: concealed, hid (stem of akhfā, "to keep hidden")

39.grammar: Past-tense verb, Form IV ("to make hidden"). The -tum ending marks the subject "you all (masculine plural)" — the standard past-tense subject suffix.

40.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
40.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

41.meaning: "You (all) declared openly / made public" — to announce, to bring something out into the open.

parts.en: declared openly (stem of aʿlana, "to make public")

41.grammar: Past-tense verb, Form IV — the causative of "being open": to make something public. The -tum suffix marks the subject "you all (masculine plural)." It is the natural opposite of akhfaytum, "you concealed."

42.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
42.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

43.meaning: "He does it" — the plain verb of doing or performing an act, with "it" attached as its object.
43.grammar: Present-tense verb with ya- ("he") and the object pronoun -hu ("it"). The stem ends without a vowel (yafʿal-, not yafʿalu) — the clipped "jussive" mood, which typically appears in conditional sentences ("whoever does it…") or after certain particles.

44.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
44.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
44.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

45.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
45.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

46.meaning: He strayed, lost the way, or went off course — to wander from the right path, whether literally or figuratively (to err, be misguided, or deviate from truth and guidance).
46.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he went astray'. The bare past-tense form with the -a ending signals a single male (or thing) as the doer of a completed action.
46.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

47.meaning: Evenness, levelness, the middle or exact center; by extension the straight, balanced, even course. When joined to a following noun it commonly yields the sense 'the very midst of' or 'the soundness/straightness of'.
47.grammar: A noun ending in -a, the accusative case. The accusative typically marks a word as the direct object of a verb, or sets it up to be joined to a following noun ('the evenness OF …').
47.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — to be even, level, equal

48.meaning: The way, road, or path — a route one travels; very often used figuratively for a course of life, conduct, or the path of religion. The attached article makes it definite: 'the way'.
48.grammar: al- is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates to the following 's', heard as 'as-sabīl'). The final -i is the genitive ending, marking the word as joined to a preceding noun ('… OF the way') or governed by a preposition.

1.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
1.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

2.meaning: "They get hold of you / gain the upper hand over you" — thaqifa means to catch, encounter, or overpower someone, to have them in one's grasp.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb: ya- plus the plural -ū marks "they," and -kum ("you all") is the attached object. The plural ends in bare -ū rather than the full -ūna: the shortened mood used after particles such as "if" — typical of conditional clauses ("if they get hold of you…").

3.meaning: To be, to become, or to come to be — the basic verb of being and existence, also used as a helper to place a statement in past or continuing time.
3.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of being, third person masculine plural ('they'). The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-party subject and the long '-ū' marks the masculine plural 'they'. The stem is bare 'kūn' with no indicative '-u' vowel, and the missing final 'n' on the ending shows subjunctive/jussive mood — typically governed by a preceding particle ('that they be…' / 'they would be').
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come into being

4.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
4.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

5.meaning: Enemies — those locked in hostility or opposition; the plural of 'enemy'.
5.grammar: A plural noun 'enemies' with the -an ending, which marks it as indefinite ('enemies') and in the accusative case. The accusative is the case used for the direct object of a verb or, very commonly, for a word that states what someone became or how they ended up ('became enemies').

6.meaning: "And they stretch out / extend" — basaṭa is to spread or stretch something out; stretching out one's hand against someone is an idiom for attacking or harming.
6.grammar: wa- ("and") joined to a present-tense verb. The plural marker is bare -ū instead of the full -ūna: the shortened mood a verb takes when it continues a clause governed by a particle such as "if," so it usually rides along with a preceding conditional verb.

7.meaning: To you / toward you (plural) — a preposition expressing motion or direction reaching a destination, joined with 'you all' as that destination.
7.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, toward'), whose ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached, plus -kum ('you all'). Together they mark the end-point or recipient of an action — the direction 'toward' or 'unto' a group.

8.meaning: Their hands — the physical hands; often figuratively the means by which one acts, strikes, or exerts force (plural of 'hand').
8.grammar: A plural noun (aydī, plural of yad, 'hand') with the attached possessive -hum ('their'). The -a vowel before the pronoun marks the accusative case, which typically signals that the word is the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

9.meaning: "And their tongues" — alsina is the plural of lisān, "tongue," the organ of speech; by extension, what people say.
9.grammar: wa- ("and") plus a plural noun with the possessive pronoun -hum ("their"). The -a before the pronoun is the accusative case ending, which generally marks the noun as the object of a verb or preposition-like word acting on it.

10.meaning: Evil, harm, or what is bad and distressing; something that brings injury, misfortune, or moral wrong. The prefixed 'bi' adds the sense 'with/by means of' the evil, so it points to evil as the instrument or object toward which something is directed.
10.grammar: A definite noun (the al- = 'the') governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which is the case automatically required after a preposition and which also links a noun to a preceding one in an 'of' relationship.

11.meaning: "And they wished / longed" — wadda is to love something and therefore wish for it; it expresses a heartfelt desire that something would happen.
11.grammar: wa- ("and") plus a past-tense verb. The -ū suffix is the past-tense subject marker "they (masculine plural)" — in the past tense the subject is shown by the ending, not by a prefix.

12.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
12.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

13.meaning: A verb meaning 'you disbelieve', 'you reject faith', or 'you are ungrateful' — to refuse to believe, to deny the truth, or to be ungrateful, addressed to a group.
13.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks the second person ('you') and the -ūna ending marks a masculine-plural subject in the indicative mood (ongoing or habitual action). The root joins the ideas of denying faith and being ungrateful — covering over a truth or a blessing.
13.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to disbelieve, deny, be ungrateful, cover over

1.meaning: 'Never / will not' — a particle that negates a future action emphatically. Lan denies that something will ever happen, stronger and more absolute than a simple 'not'.
1.grammar: A negating particle that applies to present-tense verbs to deny them in the future ('will never…'). Grammatically it also puts the following verb into the subjunctive mood, which clips that verb's ending to a short -a. Lan itself does not change.

2.meaning: "(It) will benefit you" — nafaʿa is to profit, help, or do good to someone; the subject is a feminine/plural thing (such as kin or wealth) said to be of use — or, with a negating particle, of no use.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb: the ta- prefix marks a feminine (or non-human plural) subject, and -kum ("you all") is the attached object. The -a on the stem (tanfaʿa, not tanfaʿu) is the dependent "subjunctive" mood, the form a verb takes after particles such as lan ("never will").

3.meaning: "Your kinship ties / your blood relatives" — arḥām is the plural of raḥim, "womb," used for the bonds of blood relationship that spring from it.

parts.en: wombs, kinship ties (plural of raḥim) + nominative -u

3.grammar: A plural noun with the possessive pronoun -kum ("your"). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case ending, which generally marks the noun as the subject — the one doing (or failing to do) something.

4.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
4.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

5.meaning: Your children / your offspring — the plural of walad ('child'), with the possessive suffix -kum ('your', masculine plural). It refers to one's sons and daughters.
5.grammar: A broken plural noun (jam' taksir) in the nominative case (rafi, -u ending), functioning as subject. The suffix -kum is a second-person masculine plural possessive pronoun.
5.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth to, beget; child, offspring

6.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
6.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
6.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

7.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
7.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

8.meaning: "he/it distinguishes, separates, or decides" — to draw a clear dividing line between things, and so to settle a matter or pass decisive judgment that separates truth from falsehood or one party from another.
8.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ("he/it"). The final -u is the indicative ending, the verb's plain, unmodified present-tense form stating that the action happens or will happen.
8.root: ف-ص-ل (f-ṣ-l) — to separate, divide, distinguish, decide

9.meaning: Between you / among you; the space or relation linking the members of a group.
9.grammar: An adverb of place ('between/among') with an attached pronoun. The fixed -a ending is characteristic of such place-words; the ending -kum means 'you' for a group, so the whole means 'among you all'.
9.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation/interval; the space between two things

10.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
10.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
10.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

11.meaning: A compound meaning roughly 'because of what...', 'on account of that which...', or 'by means of what...'. It joins the preposition 'with/by/because of' to a connector 'what/that which', introducing the reason or instrument for something.
11.grammar: A preposition (bi-) fused to the word mā ('what / that which'). The preposition bi- expresses cause, means, or accompaniment; combined with mā it forms a phrase pointing to the thing or fact that serves as a reason or means ('because of what...').

12.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
12.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

13.meaning: 'All-Seeing / fully observant' — one who sees clearly and with complete insight; as a divine attribute, the One who perceives all things.
13.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, denoting one who possesses sight to a high degree — 'all-seeing'. The -un ending (tanwīn) is nominative plus indefiniteness, the form used for a subject or for a predicate ('[He] is all-seeing').

1.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

2.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'she was / it was / it became' — from the core verb of being, linking a subject to a description or state, often setting it in past or established time.
2.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb of being. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine-singular subject, 'she' or 'it (feminine)', so it reads 'she/it was'. As a being-verb it normally introduces a description of that subject.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

3.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
3.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

4.meaning: Uswa — "a pattern to follow, a model example": someone whose conduct is worthy of imitation, a living template for one's own behaviour.
4.grammar: A feminine noun. The -un ending is the indefinite nominative: "an example" — the double-vowel (nunation) marks indefiniteness, and the u-vowel marks the nominative case, typical of a subject or of the thing being affirmed to exist ("there is… an example").

5.meaning: "A good thing / a benefit" — something good, beautiful, or pleasing; a good deed or a piece of good fortune.
5.grammar: A feminine singular noun/adjective. The -at ending marks it as feminine; the final -un is nominative case with tanwīn (the -n showing it is indefinite, 'a good thing'). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence.

6.meaning: The preposition 'in / within / during.' It places something inside a container, period, place, or matter.
6.grammar: A preposition. It governs the noun that follows, putting it in the genitive case and situating something inside it — in space, in time ('during'), or in a circumstance.

7.meaning: The proper name Ibrāhīm (the Prophet Abraham).
7.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -a ending here serves for both accusative and genitive because the name is a diptote — a class of nouns that refuses tanwīn (no -an/-in) and uses a single -a for these two cases. So this one -a covers 'Ibrāhīm' whether as an object or as 'of Ibrāhīm'.

8.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
8.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

9.meaning: Together with him; in his company or alongside him.
9.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment, 'with', joined to the attached pronoun -hu 'him'. Together they mean 'with him / in his company'.

10.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
10.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

11.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

12.meaning: "To their people" — qawm is a people, folk, or community: the group a person belongs to and addresses.
12.grammar: The preposition li- ("to/for") plus a noun plus the possessive pronoun -him ("their"). The -i on qawmi is the genitive case ending that a noun always takes after a preposition; the pronoun's vowel also shifts to -him (rather than -hum) to echo that i-sound.
12.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — standing; a community that stands together

13.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
13.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

14.meaning: "Free of / disassociated from" — the plural of barī', one who is clear, quit, and innocent of something, having washed his hands of it entirely.
14.grammar: A plural adjective used as a predicate: "(are) clear/quit of." The final -u is the nominative case, marking it as what is being said about the subject ("we are free of you"); this plural pattern is a diptote, so it takes -u with no nunation. The trailing alif is purely orthographic and unpronounced.

15.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
15.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
15.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

16.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and from/out of that which' or 'and from what'. It joins a new item to what precedes and points to an unspecified thing or category ('whatever it is that...').
16.grammar: A combination of the connector wa ('and'), the preposition min ('from, out of, part of'), and the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). The nūn of min has assimilated into the mīm of mā, doubling it (mim-mā). The whole phrase is invariable and does not take case endings.

17.meaning: You worship (Him) — to serve, devote oneself to, and submit in obedient adoration to a deity. The verb conveys total devotion: not merely outward ritual but the humble servitude a worshipper owes to the One worshipped.
17.grammar: Present/future-tense verb addressed to a group of males ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks second person ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural subjects and the indicative mood (a plain statement of fact, 'you do/will worship'), as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form which would drop the final -na.
17.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, submit as a devoted servant

18.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
18.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

19.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
19.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
19.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

20.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
20.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

21.meaning: 'We have disbelieved / rejected / denied.' The verb means to refuse faith, to reject the truth, and can also carry the sense of ingratitude — a covering-over and denial of what one has been given.
21.grammar: A past-tense verb. The attached -nā ending marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The past tense presents the act of disbelief or rejection as something already done.

22.meaning: A preposition 'bi' ('with / by / in / for') joined to the attached pronoun 'you all', yielding 'with you' or 'for you (plural)'. The exact shade — attachment, instrument, or benefit — depends on the verb it accompanies.
22.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. 'bi' is a versatile preposition (with, by, in, for), and -kum is the genitive/object pronoun 'you all' (masculine plural). Pronouns following a preposition always take this attached (genitive) form.

23.meaning: And (will) appear — wabadā means 'and it appeared', 'and it became manifest', describing the sudden manifestation of evil deeds and their consequences on Judgment Day.

parts.en: it appeared, it became manifest, it was exposed

23.grammar: Wa- is the conjunction. Badā is Form I perfect (third masculine singular) from root b-d-w/b-d-y, meaning to appear, to become manifest, to be revealed. The alif maqṣūra marks the weak root. Context: 'And the evil of what they did appeared to them' — on Judgment Day, their evil deeds will be openly exposed.
23.root: ب-د-و/ي (b-d-w/y) — to appear, to become visible, to be manifest

24.meaning: 'Between us' — the spatial or relational word for 'between/among', with 'us' attached: the space, relation, or matter standing between ourselves.
24.grammar: An adverb of place 'between', fixed in the -a form, with the attached pronoun -na ('us'). Together they mean 'between us / among us', marking a relation linking two or more parties.
24.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

25.meaning: "And between you" — bayna is the word for the space or relation "between" two parties.
25.grammar: wa- ("and") plus the adverb bayna ("between"), which always ends in the fixed -a of adverbs of place, plus the pronoun -kum ("you all"). The extra -u on -kumu is just a helping vowel to link smoothly to a following word beginning with "al-."

26.meaning: "The enmity" — ʿadāwa is open, active hostility: the settled state of being enemies.
26.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The final -u is the nominative case ending, generally marking the word as the subject of its sentence — the thing that "appears" or "exists." The tā' (-t-) is the feminine noun ending.

27.meaning: "And the hatred" — baghḍā' is intense loathing, deep-seated detestation of someone; stronger and more visceral than ʿadāwa (enmity).
27.grammar: wa- ("and") linking this noun to a previous one, so it shares that noun's role. The final -u is the nominative case ending, marking it as (part of) the subject; the word's long-ā' feminine pattern makes it a diptote, so it takes no nunation.

28.meaning: An adverb meaning 'ever / forever / at any time' — used to stress that something will never (or always) be the case throughout all time, especially with a negative to mean 'never, not ever'.
28.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative, the form regularly used to turn a word into an adverb of time ('… ever / forever'); the -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite. Paired with a negation it strengthens it to 'never, not ever'.

29.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
29.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

30.meaning: You (plural) believe — to have faith, to trust and affirm as true, especially trust in Allah and what He has revealed; also to be secure or to grant security.
30.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the form meaning 'to have faith'. The 'tu-' prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the shortened '-ū' ending (without final 'na') indicates the subjunctive/jussive mood — the form used after certain particles such as 'that', 'in order to', 'if', or negation.

31.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
31.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
31.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

32.meaning: "Him alone" — waḥd is "aloneness, being one"; with the pronoun it forms the fixed expression "He alone / only Him," singling out one to the exclusion of all others.
32.grammar: The noun waḥd ("aloneness") frozen in the accusative -a, which here works adverbially — "in a state of being alone" — plus the pronoun -hu ("him"). The whole word functions as "him alone / exclusively," always in this fixed adverbial shape.

33.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
33.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

34.meaning: The saying, statement, or utterance — speech that is spoken; a word, remark, or what someone says.
34.grammar: A noun, 'saying/speech.' The final -a ending is the accusative case, which commonly marks the noun as the direct object — the thing the verb acts upon (e.g., what is heard, said, or known). This form names the act or product of speaking.
34.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak; an utterance

35.meaning: The proper name Ibrāhīm (the Prophet Abraham).
35.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -a ending here serves for both accusative and genitive because the name is a diptote — a class of nouns that refuses tanwīn (no -an/-in) and uses a single -a for these two cases. So this one -a covers 'Ibrāhīm' whether as an object or as 'of Ibrāhīm'.

36.meaning: To / for his father — the noun 'father' attached to a possessive 'his' and preceded by the preposition 'to/for.'
36.grammar: Preposition + noun + possessive pronoun. The li- prefix means 'to' or 'for.' 'Father' is one of a small group of nouns that show case with a long vowel: the -ī here reflects the genitive required after the preposition. The attached -hi means 'his' (its 'i' vowel harmonizes after the preceding -ī).

37.meaning: "I will most surely ask forgiveness" — istaghfara is to seek forgiveness, to plead that wrongs be pardoned; here wrapped in double emphasis: "truly, I shall certainly seek forgiveness."

parts.en: seek forgiveness (Form X stem: "ask to be forgiven")

37.grammar: A doubly emphatic present-tense verb: the la- prefix means "surely," the a- marks "I," the ista- pattern (Form X) means "to seek" the root's meaning — to seek ghafr, forgiveness — and the heavy -anna ending is the "nūn of emphasis" used in solemn promises and oaths: "I will most certainly…"

38.meaning: 'For You / to You' — a 'for/to' particle attached to the pronoun 'You,' indicating that something is directed toward, or done for the sake of, a single addressee.
38.grammar: A small phrase: the particle li- ('for / to,' vowelled la- before a pronoun) joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'you' (one masculine addressee). The pronoun is in the form used as the object of a preposition, marking the person as the one to whom or for whom the action is directed.

39.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
39.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

40.meaning: 'I own / I control / I have power over'. A verb expressing that the speaker possesses, has authority over, or is able to dispose of something.
40.grammar: Present-tense verb with the 'I' prefix (a-) at the front meaning the speaker does the action. The -u ending is the plain indicative, used for a simple statement of fact ('I do / I am doing').
40.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, possess, have power

41.meaning: 'For You / to You' — a 'for/to' particle attached to the pronoun 'You,' indicating that something is directed toward, or done for the sake of, a single addressee.
41.grammar: A small phrase: the particle li- ('for / to,' vowelled la- before a pronoun) joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'you' (one masculine addressee). The pronoun is in the form used as the object of a preposition, marking the person as the one to whom or for whom the action is directed.

42.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
42.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

43.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
43.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

44.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
44.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

45.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
45.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
45.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

46.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

46.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
46.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

47.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
47.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

48.meaning: 'We have placed our trust, relied wholly (upon someone).' The root means to entrust an affair, to depend on and commit oneself; this pattern expresses fully delegating one's reliance. The subject is 'we.'
48.grammar: A past-tense verb in a reflexive pattern ('to commit one's reliance, put one's trust'). The suffix -nā marks the subject 'we' ('we put our trust').
48.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, rely upon, commit an affair

49.meaning: "and to You / and toward You" — wa- joins it on; ilā is the preposition 'to / toward,' and the attached -ka means 'You,' giving 'to You' (a direction or destination).
49.grammar: A preposition ('to/toward') with an attached pronoun. The base ilā shifts to ilay- before a pronoun, and -ka means 'you' (one person addressed). Prepositions like this point to a direction or destination.

50.meaning: "We have turned in devotion" — the verb anāba means to turn back to Allah again and again in repentance and humble reliance, returning to Him as one's true refuge.

parts.en: turned back in repentance (Form IV of the root, 'to return devotedly')

50.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The -nā ending is the subject pronoun 'we': it marks that the doers are a group including the speaker — 'we turned'. The middle long vowel of anāba shrinks to a short a (anab-) whenever a consonant-starting ending like -nā is attached; this is normal for verbs with a weak middle root letter.
50.root: ن-و-ب (n-w-b) — to return repeatedly, turn back to

51.meaning: "and to You / and toward You" — wa- joins it on; ilā is the preposition 'to / toward,' and the attached -ka means 'You,' giving 'to You' (a direction or destination).
51.grammar: A preposition ('to/toward') with an attached pronoun. The base ilā shifts to ilay- before a pronoun, and -ka means 'you' (one person addressed). Prepositions like this point to a direction or destination.

52.meaning: Al-maṣīr — the destination, the place or state one finally comes to; the journey's end or ultimate outcome to which things return.
52.grammar: A definite noun of place/result on the pattern mafʿil, with the long ī arising from the weak root letter yāʾ (ص-ي-ر). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or what something ultimately is. The word denotes the final place or state to which one comes.
52.root: ص-ي-ر (ṣ-y-r) — to become, come to, end up at

1.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

1.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
1.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: You place us / make us: a present-tense verb of putting, setting, or rendering something into a state, with an attached pronoun 'us' as its object.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with no plural ending marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The bare (vowelless) ending shows the jussive mood, the form used after particles of command or prohibition. The attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us.'
3.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

4.meaning: A trial, test, temptation, affliction, or sedition. Fitna is a weighty term: originally the smelting of metal to test its purity, it comes to mean any testing or tribulation — persecution, civil strife, seductive enticement, or a probing ordeal that reveals what is within.
4.grammar: An indefinite feminine noun. The ending -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a trial') and in the accusative case — typically the case of a direct object or of a noun functioning as the predicate after certain verbs.
4.root: ف-ت-ن (f-t-n) — to test by fire, to try, to tempt, to afflict

5.meaning: 'For/to those who …' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the masculine plural relative pronoun 'those who,' which introduces a description of a group by something they do.
5.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to') fused with the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). Relative pronouns like this do not change for case; they point ahead to a clause that describes the group ('those who …').

6.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
6.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

7.meaning: "and forgive / and cover over" — wa- joins it on; the verb means to forgive, to cover over and shield a sin so it is not exposed or held against the person.
7.grammar: A command/request verb addressed to one person ('forgive!'). The bare consonant ending (-fir, no end-vowel) is the command form, and the helping vowel at the start (i-) lets the cluster be pronounced; it asks the one addressed to perform the act.
7.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, shield; to forgive, pardon

8.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
8.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

9.meaning: An address to Allah meaning 'Our Lord' — invoking the Sustainer, Master, and Nurturer who creates, owns, provides for, and brings His servants to maturity. 'Rabb' is a rich term: not merely 'lord' but the One who cherishes and governs all that He has made. The attached 'our' makes it a direct calling upon Him.
9.grammar: A noun ('Lord / Sustainer') with an attached possessive pronoun. The -a ending reflects the accusative, used here in the vocative sense (calling out, 'O our Lord') — the implied 'O' (yā) is dropped before a noun joined to a pronoun. The suffix -nā means 'our'. So it reads 'O our Lord / our Lord!'.
9.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship and cherishing care

10.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
10.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

11.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
11.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

12.meaning: "the All-Mighty / the Ever-Dominant" — one who is mighty, invincible, and held in honour; as a divine name 'al-ʿAzīz' denotes the One who is supremely powerful, unconquerable, and exalted above all.
12.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a strong, enduring quality. The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

13.meaning: The All-Wise — one possessing perfect wisdom, who puts everything in its right place and acts with flawless judgment; can also carry the sense of one who decrees and decides soundly.
13.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) stressing the depth and constancy of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a describing predicate.
13.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge wisely, to be wise

1.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
1.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
3.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

4.meaning: "in them / among them" — the preposition 'in/among' joined to the pronoun 'them,' locating something within or amid a group of people.
4.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun, giving 'fīhim.' The preposition 'fī' keeps its long 'ī.' The pronoun '-him' is the third-person masculine plural ('them'); its vowel is 'i' (rather than '-hum') because it follows the high front vowel 'ī' of 'fī'.
4.root: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

5.meaning: Uswa — "a pattern to follow, a model example": someone whose conduct is worthy of imitation, a living template for one's own behaviour.
5.grammar: A feminine noun. The -un ending is the indefinite nominative: "an example" — the double-vowel (nunation) marks indefiniteness, and the u-vowel marks the nominative case, typical of a subject or of the thing being affirmed to exist ("there is… an example").

6.meaning: "A good thing / a benefit" — something good, beautiful, or pleasing; a good deed or a piece of good fortune.
6.grammar: A feminine singular noun/adjective. The -at ending marks it as feminine; the final -un is nominative case with tanwīn (the -n showing it is indefinite, 'a good thing'). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence.

7.meaning: A combined expression meaning 'to whom?' or 'for whom?' — it asks about the owner or the one to whom something belongs. It fuses the preposition 'to/for' with the question word 'who'.
7.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') joined to the interrogative 'who'. Together they pose the question 'to whom (does it belong)?'. The combination is fixed in form and does not change its ending.

8.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

8.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

9.meaning: He hopes for, looks forward to, or expectantly desires something good; it can also carry the nuance of awe or fearful expectation. The verb blends hopeful longing with anticipation of what is to come.

parts.en: spelling alif after the long ū

9.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he hopes'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he' subject; the stem ends in a long -ū. The written alif at the end is a spelling convention (it is not pronounced) and does not change the meaning. The form describes an ongoing or habitual action.
9.root: ر-ج-و (r-j-w) — hoping, expecting, looking forward to good

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
10.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

11.meaning: "And the Day" — al-yawm is the day; with 'the' it very often points to the momentous Day, i.e. the Last Day, the Day of Judgment.
11.grammar: A noun with 'and' and 'the' attached. The final -a is the accusative case ending: it typically marks the word as the object of a verb or hope/expectation ('hopes for the Day'), or as an adverb of time ('on the day'). It is not the subject form (-u) or the 'of'-form (-i).

12.meaning: "The Last / the Final" — ākhir is what comes at the end; with 'the Day' it names the Last Day, the final Day toward which all things run.
12.grammar: An adjective made definite by al- 'the'. The final -a is the accusative ending: it typically marks the word as (or as describing) the object of a verb — an adjective takes the same case as the noun it describes.
12.root: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, come after

13.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
13.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

14.meaning: "He takes as an ally / turns to in alliance," or simply "turns away," from a verb meaning to turn toward something and befriend/ally with it — or, with the opposite nuance, to turn one's back on it.

parts.en: take as ally / turn to (or away)

14.grammar: The "ya-" prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ("he") in the present-future tense. With the weak final letter dropped (leaving a short "-a"), the verb is in the jussive/subjunctive mood, the form triggered by certain conditional or governing particles. The verb is the reflexive Form V (tafaʿʿala), "to turn oneself toward / take for oneself as ally."
14.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, alliance; to turn toward, befriend, take charge (or, turn away)

15.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
15.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

16.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
16.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

17.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
17.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

18.meaning: The Self-Sufficient / the Free-of-Need / the Rich — the One utterly independent and in need of nothing, possessing all wealth; as a human trait it means rich or free from want.
18.grammar: An intensive adjective on the 'faʿīl' pattern (denoting a deep, established quality), with 'the'. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as a subject or the thing being described.
18.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, self-sufficient

19.grammar: adjective used as Divine Name, intensive form (فَعِيل pattern), masculine singular, nominative case, definite with article; one of the Names of Allah

1.meaning: It may be / perhaps. A verb expressing hope or expectation that something will come about — 'it is to be hoped that…'.
1.grammar: A verb of 'hoping/expectation' that often functions like the particle 'perhaps', introducing an anticipated outcome (usually followed by a clause stating what is hoped for). It is a defective (final-weak) triliteral verb and can take person-marked endings — e.g., ʿasaytum ('you [pl.] may'), ʿasaynā ('we may') — so it is not invariable. The bare third-person masculine singular form ʿasā shown here is its most common usage.
1.root: ع-س-و / ع-س-ي (ʿ-s-w / ʿ-s-y) — to hope for, to be near/likely; the final-weak root underlying 'perhaps, it may be'

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'he makes', 'he appoints', 'he places', or 'he assigns' — a versatile verb of bringing something into a state, position, or role.
4.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'), marked by 'ya-'. The '-a' ending is the subjunctive mood, which typically appears after particles meaning 'that', 'so that', 'in order to', or 'will not' — expressing a dependent or intended action rather than a plain fact.
4.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, place, appoint

5.meaning: Between you / among you; the space or relation linking the members of a group.
5.grammar: An adverb of place ('between/among') with an attached pronoun. The fixed -a ending is characteristic of such place-words; the ending -kum means 'you' for a group, so the whole means 'among you all'.
5.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation/interval; the space between two things

6.meaning: 'And between'. A connective word meaning 'and between / and amid', used to mark the space, relationship, or distinction lying among two or more parties.
6.grammar: The word bayna ('between') with 'and' in front. It is an adverb of place that always leads into what follows, so it ends in a fixed -a and is normally paired with a following noun or pronoun ('between … and …').

7.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
7.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

8.meaning: "You have shown enmity to" — the Form III verb ʿādā means to set oneself against someone, to treat them as an enemy in an ongoing, mutual hostility.

parts.en: acted with enmity toward (Form III: directed hostility at someone)

8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The -tum ending is the subject pronoun 'you (plural, addressing men or a mixed group)': it marks that the addressees did the action. The stem's final weak letter appears as -ay- before this consonant-starting ending (ʿāday-tum), a regular change in verbs ending in a weak root letter.

9.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
9.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'affection, love, fond attachment' — warm goodwill and tender liking between people.
10.grammar: A feminine verbal noun on the pattern mafʿala. The -an ending (with tanwīn on the tā' marbūṭa, hence -tan) is the indefinite accusative: it typically marks the noun as an object of a verb, or as a specifying complement ('… in respect of …').

11.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
11.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
11.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

12.meaning: 'All-Powerful,' 'fully able,' 'one who has complete power and capability.' An intensive form expressing that the one described possesses perfect, unrestricted power to do whatever is willed — a quality applied supremely to Allah.
12.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, established capability. The '-un' ending (tanwīn al-ḍamm) marks the nominative case (the 'subject/predicate' case) together with indefiniteness — typically the role of a subject or, very often, a predicate describing who or what something is.

13.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
13.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
13.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

14.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.

15.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
15.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').

1.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
1.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

2.meaning: "He forbids you" — the verb nahā means to prohibit, to hold someone back from an action, declaring it off-limits.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix means 'he/it' (a masculine singular doer). The attached -kum means 'you (plural)' as the object of the forbidding. The extra final -u on -kumu is just a helping vowel that Arabic adds to -kum when the next word begins with a joining (silent) alif; it carries no meaning of its own.

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
