3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
4.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

5.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
5.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

6.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

6.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'they fight/wage combat against you (a plural group).' Built on Form III (qātala), which conveys mutual, reciprocal action — fighting back and forth between two parties, i.e. warfare or armed struggle.
7.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The yu- prefix with the -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The final -ū here lacks the long nūn of the indicative, signalling that the verb is in a subjunctive/jussive mood (typically after a particle or conditional). The attached -kum is the object 'you (plural).'
7.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, fight, do battle

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: 'the religion / the way of life' — dīn denotes religion in the full sense: a system of belief, worship, obedience, and a complete way of living; it also carries the senses of judgement and requital, the order one is accountable to.
9.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -i ending is genitive: this case typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive-type relationship ('… of …').

10.meaning: 'And not' — the conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lam, a particle that negates a verb and pushes its meaning into the completed past ('did not …').
10.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus the negative particle lam. Lam negates a following present-tense verb but turns its sense into the past: 'has not / did not …'. It also causes that verb to take the jussive (clipped) ending.

11.meaning: "That they drive you out / expel you" — Form IV akhraja means to make someone go out, to force them from their homes or land.

parts.en: drive out, expel (Form IV: cause to go out) + plural 'they'

11.grammar: A present-tense verb: yu- ... -ū together mean 'they (a group of men) do'. Notice the plural ending is bare -ū, not -ūna: the dropped final -na is the sign of the 'dependent' (subjunctive/jussive) mood, used after little particles like 'that', 'so that', 'not', or 'did not'. The -kum after it is the object pronoun 'you (plural)'.

12.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
12.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

13.meaning: Your homes / your dwellings — the abodes belonging to the addressed group. 'diyār' is the plural of 'dār' (home, abode, dwelling-place).
13.grammar: A plural noun ('homes') with the attached possessive pronoun '-kum' (your, for a group). The -i ending before the suffix marks the genitive case — typically because the word follows a preposition or stands in a possessive 'of' link.
13.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to turn, encircle; an enclosed dwelling, abode, home

14.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
14.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

15.meaning: "That you treat them with dutiful kindness" — the verb barra means to be good, loyal and generously kind toward someone, the same warm dutifulness (birr) owed to parents.

parts.en: act with kindness and dutiful goodness + plural 'you all'

15.grammar: A present-tense verb: ta- ... -ū together mean 'you (plural) do'. The plural ending is bare -ū with no final -na: the missing -na marks the 'dependent' (subjunctive) mood that follows particles like 'that' ('that you be kind…'). The -hum ending is the object pronoun 'them (masculine)'.

16.meaning: "And that you act justly" — Form IV aqsaṭa means to deal with scrupulous fairness, to give everyone their equitable due (qisṭ = just measure).

parts.en: act justly, deal equitably (Form IV) + plural 'you all'

16.grammar: 'And' plus a present-tense verb: tu- ... -ū together mean 'you (plural) do'. The bare -ū ending without a final -na is the 'dependent' (subjunctive) mood, the form a plural verb takes after particles like 'that' — so it reads 'that you deal justly'. The silent final alif in the spelling is just Arabic writing convention after a plural -ū.

17.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
17.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
17.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

18.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
18.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
19.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

20.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
20.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
20.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

21.meaning: A noun (plural) meaning 'those who act justly / the equitable ones' — people who deal fairly and give everyone their due, establishing balance and justice. The form names them as doers of just dealing.

parts.en: one who acts justly (form IV agent)

21.grammar: A doer-noun (active participle, form IV — 'one who deals equitably') with the definite article 'al-,' made plural with the -īna ending. The -īna marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive case — the form used when the noun is a direct object or follows a preposition, as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject.

1.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
1.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

2.meaning: "He forbids you" — the verb nahā means to prohibit, to hold someone back from an action, declaring it off-limits.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix means 'he/it' (a masculine singular doer). The attached -kum means 'you (plural)' as the object of the forbidding. The extra final -u on -kumu is just a helping vowel that Arabic adds to -kum when the next word begins with a joining (silent) alif; it carries no meaning of its own.

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
4.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

5.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
5.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'they fought you (a plural group).' Form III (qātala) denotes reciprocal combat — two sides engaging one another in battle.
6.grammar: A past/perfect verb. The -ū ending marks a completed action done by a third-person masculine plural subject ('they did…'). The attached -kum is the object 'you (plural).' The perfect tense presents the act as finished or established.
6.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, fight, do battle

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: 'the religion / the way of life' — dīn denotes religion in the full sense: a system of belief, worship, obedience, and a complete way of living; it also carries the senses of judgement and requital, the order one is accountable to.
8.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -i ending is genitive: this case typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive-type relationship ('… of …').

9.meaning: "And they drove you out" — the completed act of expelling people from their homes or homeland.

parts.en: drove out, expelled (Form IV: made go out)

9.grammar: 'And' plus a past-tense (perfect) verb. The -ū ending on a past-tense verb is the subject pronoun 'they (a group of men)': it marks who did the action. The -kum after it is the object pronoun 'you (plural)' — the ones the action was done to.

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

11.meaning: Your homes / your dwellings — the abodes belonging to the addressed group. 'diyār' is the plural of 'dār' (home, abode, dwelling-place).
11.grammar: A plural noun ('homes') with the attached possessive pronoun '-kum' (your, for a group). The -i ending before the suffix marks the genitive case — typically because the word follows a preposition or stands in a possessive 'of' link.
11.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to turn, encircle; an enclosed dwelling, abode, home

12.meaning: "And they backed / gave support" — Form III ẓāhara literally means to lend someone your back (ẓahr): to reinforce, aid and side with a party, especially against others.
12.grammar: 'And' plus a past-tense (perfect) verb. The -ū ending is the subject pronoun 'they (a group of men)' on a past-tense verb: it tells you a group performed the completed action. The silent alif written after it is only a spelling convention, not a sound.
12.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — back; to appear, to back/support

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
13.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').

14.meaning: "Your being driven out / your expulsion" — ikhrāj is the action-noun of Form IV akhraja: the act of forcing someone out.

parts.en: expulsion, driving out (action noun) + genitive ending

14.grammar: A verbal noun ('the act of expelling') with an attached possessor. The -i before the pronoun is the genitive case ending: it typically appears when the word follows a preposition or is linked to another word by 'of'. The -kum ending means 'your (plural)' — and with an action noun it can name either the doers or, as often, the ones the action is done to ('the expelling OF you').

15.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
15.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

16.meaning: "That you take them as close allies" — Form V tawallā means to turn toward someone and attach yourself to them, giving them your loyalty, friendship and protective alliance (walāyah).

parts.en: you (present tense; one of two original ta- syllables, the second dropped for lightness)
turn to in loyalty, take as ally (Form V) + plural 'you all' (-aw)

16.grammar: A present-tense verb of the pattern tatawallaw, with one of the doubled ta- syllables dropped — a common lightening in this verb type. The plural 'you' ending appears as -aw (because the stem ends in a weak letter) with no final -na: that missing -na is the sign of the 'dependent' (subjunctive/jussive) mood used after particles like 'that' or 'not'. The -hum is the object pronoun 'them'.

17.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
17.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

18.meaning: He takes (someone) as a close ally, befriends and allies himself with them, gives them his loyalty and turns to them for support. The Form V verb adds the sense of deliberately choosing and embracing that allegiance for oneself.

parts.en: take as ally (Form V, reflexive stem)

18.grammar: A present-tense Form V verb for 'he', with the attached object pronoun -hum ('them'). The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject; the long -ā stem is characteristic of this verb pattern, and -hum names the people receiving the action.

19.meaning: So those / then those are the ones — a connector 'so/then' joined to a demonstrative pointing to a distant or already-mentioned group: 'those people, they (are the ones who)…'.
19.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', often introducing a result or consequence. 'ulā'ika' is a plural demonstrative ('those') pointing to people, typically picking up a previously described group and setting them up as the subject. It is fixed in form and does not change for case.

20.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
20.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

21.meaning: The wrongdoers; those who do wrong, act unjustly, or place things where they do not belong. The underlying image is one who oppresses, transgresses limits, and deals unjustly with others or with themselves.
21.grammar: An active participle (the doer of the action) made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative (subject) case, the form used when the word functions as the doer of a verb or the subject of a sentence.

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: They believed, they came to faith; to place trust and security in something and affirm it as true (the inner act of faith).
3.grammar: A past-tense verb of the Form IV (causative) pattern. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') for a completed action ('they believed'). The final written alif after the wāw is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

5.meaning: 'he/it came to you' — the arrival of someone or something to a group of people addressed.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb ('came'), done by 'he/it'. The verb is intransitive, so the attached -kum ('you,' plural) is not a direct object but a recipient/directional pronoun marking the people the arrival is toward ('came to you'); it is voweled -kumu before a following word. So: 'he/it came to you (all).'

6.meaning: "The believing women" — the feminine plural of mu'min, one who has īmān: settled faith and trust in Allah that brings inner security.

parts.en: believing (one who has faith; doer-form of Form IV 'to believe')

6.grammar: 'The' plus a feminine sound plural noun. The -āt ending marks a plural of women or feminine things. The final -u is the nominative case ending: it typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence — the one doing or being something ('the believing women come…').

7.meaning: "Emigrant women" — feminine plural of muhājir, one who performs hijrah: leaving home and homeland, cutting ties with a place, for the sake of Allah.

parts.en: emigrating, one who migrates (doer-form of Form III 'to emigrate')
feminine plural marker + indefinite case ending

7.grammar: A feminine sound plural noun without 'the'. The -āt marks a plural of women. The final -in (double kasrah, tanwīn) does two jobs: the 'n' sound marks indefiniteness ('some emigrant women', not 'the'), and the -i vowel is the non-subject case — on this feminine plural pattern the same -i ending serves both for 'of/after a preposition' uses and for object/state uses ('as emigrants').

8.meaning: "Then test them (the women)" — Form VIII imtaḥana means to examine and put to the test to discern what is genuine (the same root as miḥnah, a trial).

parts.en: test, examine (Form VIII: probe to verify)

8.grammar: 'Then' plus a command (imperative) verb. The -ū ending on an imperative addresses a group: 'you all, do it!'. The -hunna ending is the feminine plural object pronoun 'them (women)'. The initial i- of imtaḥin- is a mere helping vowel to start the consonant cluster, which is why it is written with a joining alif.
8.root: م-ح-ن (m-ḥ-n) — to test, put on trial

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
9.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

10.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
10.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.

11.meaning: "Concerning their (the women's) faith" — īmān is inward belief and trust in Allah, faith that gives security to the heart; bi- ties another word to it ('with/about their faith').

parts.en: faith, belief (action-noun of Form IV 'to believe') + genitive ending

11.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/about') fused to a noun. The -i on īmāni is the genitive case ending, exactly what a noun takes after a preposition. The -hinna ending is the feminine plural possessor pronoun 'their (women's)'; its vowel is -hinna rather than -hunna because it follows an i-sound.

12.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
12.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

13.meaning: "You come to know them (the women)" — ʿalima is to know with certainty, to have real knowledge of something rather than assumption.

parts.en: you (plural subject; -tum lengthened to -tumū before an attached pronoun)

13.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The -tum ending is the subject 'you (plural)'; Arabic stretches it to -tumū whenever another pronoun is attached directly after it. The -hunna ending is the feminine plural object pronoun 'them (women)'. So the one word says: you (all) – knew – them.

14.meaning: "Believing women" — women possessing īmān, genuine faith and trust in Allah; the same word as al-mu'minātu but without 'the'.

parts.en: believing (one who has faith; doer-form of Form IV 'to believe')
feminine plural marker + indefinite case ending

14.grammar: A feminine sound plural noun, indefinite. The -āt marks a plural of women. The final -in (tanwīn) signals 'a/some' rather than 'the'; its -i vowel is the non-subject case, which on this feminine plural pattern covers both the 'of/after a preposition' role and the object/state role ('found to BE believers').

15.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
15.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

16.meaning: "(Do not) send them (the women) back" — rajaʿa is to return; used transitively of people it means to send or hand someone back to where they came from.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb: ta- ... -ū together mean 'you (plural) do'. The plural ending is bare -ū with no final -na: the dropped -na is the mark of the 'clipped' (jussive/subjunctive) mood that plural verbs take after words like 'do not' or 'that'. The -hunna is the feminine plural object pronoun 'them (women)'.

17.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
17.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

18.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth. The plural form (kuffār) stresses persistent, often defiant denial; the root sense is 'to cover/conceal,' hence to deny what is true and be ungrateful.
18.grammar: A definite plural noun (intensive pattern fuʿʿāl) with the article al- ('the'). The final -i is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of the disbelievers') or follows a preposition.
18.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to disbelieve, be ungrateful

19.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
19.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

20.meaning: 'They / them' — the detached subject pronoun for a group of females, standing on its own to mean 'they (feminine)' or to emphasize the female group as the topic.
20.grammar: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' for a group of females. Because it is a separate word, it normally serves as the subject of a sentence or gives emphasis ('they themselves'). Its form is fixed and does not take case endings.

21.meaning: Lawful, permitted, allowed — that which is religiously sanctioned and free to be used or done; the opposite of forbidden (ḥarām).
21.grammar: A verbal noun used with the sense 'lawful/permitted.' The final '-un' (tanwīn ḍamma) is the indefinite nominative: it marks the word as unspecified ('a permitted thing') and as nominative, the form typically used for the subject or predicate of a sentence.
21.root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — to untie, make lawful; to be permitted

22.meaning: 'For them / to them / theirs' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the pronoun 'them,' expressing that something pertains, belongs, or is owed to that group.
22.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to'), whose vowel becomes -a before an attached pronoun, joined to -hum ('them'). It commonly expresses possession or benefit — 'theirs / for them.' Particles like this carry no case or tense of their own.

23.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
23.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

24.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
24.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

25.meaning: "They are lawful" — ḥalla means to be permitted, ḥalāl: religiously allowed and free of prohibition (the root picture is 'untying' a knot of restriction).
25.grammar: A present-tense verb: ya- ... -ūna together mean 'they (a group) are/do'. Here the plural ending keeps its full form -ūna with the final -na intact: that intact -na is the sign of the plain statement (indicative) mood — a straightforward 'they are lawful', not governed by 'that' or 'not'.
25.root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — to be lawful; to untie, release

26.meaning: 'For them / to them' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a feminine-plural 'them'.
26.grammar: The preposition li- ('for, to') with an attached object pronoun -hunna ('them', feminine plural). It expresses that something belongs to, is owed to, or is on behalf of a group of females. (The vowel appears as 'la-' before the pronoun.)

27.meaning: "And give them" — Form IV ātā means to hand over, to give or grant something to someone.

parts.en: give, hand over (Form IV of 'to come': make something come to someone)

27.grammar: 'And' plus a command (imperative) verb. The -ū ending addresses a group: 'you all, give!'. The -hum ending is the object pronoun 'them (masculine)' — the recipients. The verb's weak final root letter disappears before the -ū, which is why the stem looks so short (āt-ū).
27.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (Form IV) to bring, give

28.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
28.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

29.meaning: 'They spent / disbursed' — the act of laying out wealth, giving it away, or expending it, done by a group in the past.
29.grammar: A past-tense verb in a pattern meaning to spend or expend (especially wealth). The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the silent alif written after it is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.

30.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
30.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

31.meaning: Blame, sin, or fault — moral liability incurred by a wrong action; the sense of wrongdoing that counts against a person, or any leaning toward error.
31.grammar: A masculine noun. The final -a is the accusative case ending; this ending appears, among other uses, on the noun governed by a negating particle (as in the common construction 'there is no blame …').
31.root: ج-ن-ح (j-n-ḥ) — to incline, lean, tilt (toward wrong); hence fault/sin

32.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
32.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

33.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
33.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

34.meaning: You marry them — you take them (a feminine group) in marriage, entering the marriage contract.
34.grammar: Present-tense Form I verb, second-person masculine plural, in the subjunctive/jussive mood — shown by the bare -ū ending (the indicative -ūna has dropped its final -na), which typically follows particles meaning 'to', 'that', or 'if'. The attached -hunna is the object 'them' (females).
34.root: ن-ك-ح (n-k-ḥ) — to marry, enter the marriage bond

35.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
35.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

36.meaning: A full compound verb: 'you (men) have given them (women).' It states that a group of males bestowed or handed something over to a group of females.
36.grammar: A past-tense verb of Form IV (ātā, 'to give, bring to'). The subject ending -tum means 'you (masculine plural) did'; its vowel is here stretched to -tumū to carry the following object. The object pronoun -hunna means 'them' (a group of females). So the whole reads 'you all gave them.'
36.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (Form IV) to bring, give, bestow

37.meaning: A word meaning 'their wages / dues / rewards,' referring to a group of females. The base noun is the plural of 'wage, recompense, due reward,' joined to a 'their' (feminine) possessor.
37.grammar: A 'broken' plural noun (of ajr, 'wage/reward') carrying the accusative case-vowel -a, the ending used for the object of a verb. The suffix -hunna means 'their' for a group of females. The word denotes compensation or a rightful due owed in return for something.

38.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
38.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

39.meaning: "(Do not) hold on / keep hold" — Form IV amsaka means to grasp and retain something, to keep it in your grip rather than let it go.

parts.en: hold on to, retain (Form IV) + plural 'you all'

39.grammar: A present-tense verb: tu- ... -ū together mean 'you (plural) do'. The plural ending is bare -ū without the final -na: that dropped -na is the 'clipped' (jussive/subjunctive) mood used after words like 'do not' or 'that' — typical of a prohibition ('do not keep hold…'). The silent final alif is only a spelling convention after plural -ū.

40.meaning: "To the bonds of" — ʿiṣam is the plural of ʿiṣmah: a protective tie or bond that holds fast; used of the marriage tie that binds husband and wife.

parts.en: bonds, protective ties (plural of ʿiṣmah) + genitive ending

40.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/onto') fused to a plural noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, required after a preposition; and because the noun carries a plain -i with no 'n' (no tanwīn), it is in a construct chain — expecting a following word to complete it as '…bonds OF …'.
40.root: ع-ص-م (ʿ-ṣ-m) — to protect, hold fast, preserve

41.meaning: "The disbelieving women" — kawāfir is the plural of kāfirah, a woman who practices kufr: covering over and rejecting the truth of Allah after it reaches her.

parts.en: disbelieving women (broken plural of kāfirah) + genitive ending

41.grammar: 'The' plus a broken (internally reshaped) plural referring to women. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically links the word to a preceding noun with 'of' ('the bonds OF the disbelieving women') or follows a preposition. Kawāfir is a pattern that would resist tanwīn when indefinite, but with 'the' it takes the ordinary -i.
41.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, be ungrateful, disbelieve

42.meaning: And ask, request, or inquire — a command to put a question to someone or to ask for something.
42.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a masculine plural ('you all'), prefixed with 'and'. The -ū ending marks the plural addressees. The base verb means 'to ask/request', and the imperative form directs the listeners to carry out that action.

43.meaning: A word meaning 'what' or 'that which' — a relative/indefinite particle pointing to an unspecified thing ('what', 'whatever', 'that which').
43.grammar: An invariable particle (mā) with no case ending. Depending on context it works as a relative pronoun ('that which') introducing a clause, or as an interrogative/indefinite ('what'). It does not inflect for case, gender, or number.

44.meaning: To spend, expend, or disburse — to lay out wealth or resources, often for the sake of others or a cause.
44.grammar: A past-tense verb from a causative pattern (to cause wealth to go out, i.e. to spend). The ending -tum marks a masculine plural doer, 'you all'.
44.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, to expend; expenditure

45.meaning: "And let them ask" — sa'ala is to ask, request, or demand; with the little lām of command it becomes a directive aimed at a third party: 'let them ask / they must ask'.

parts.en: they ask, request (ya- = 'they' with the -ū ending)

45.grammar: A command directed at a third party: wa 'and' + the command-lām l- 'let/must' + a present-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the plural -ū means 'they (a group of men)'. The -ū has no final -na because the command-lām puts the verb in the 'clipped' (jussive) mood — the mood of commands and prohibitions. The silent final alif is spelling convention only.

46.meaning: A word meaning 'what' or 'that which' — a relative/indefinite particle pointing to an unspecified thing ('what', 'whatever', 'that which').
46.grammar: An invariable particle (mā) with no case ending. Depending on context it works as a relative pronoun ('that which') introducing a clause, or as an interrogative/indefinite ('what'). It does not inflect for case, gender, or number.

47.meaning: 'They spent / disbursed' — the act of laying out wealth, giving it away, or expending it, done by a group in the past.
47.grammar: A past-tense verb in a pattern meaning to spend or expend (especially wealth). The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the silent alif written after it is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.

48.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' addressed to a group of people (plural 'you'). It points to something at a distance — whether physical, or to a previously mentioned matter — and is directed at multiple listeners.
48.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for something distant. The base 'dhā' carries the sense 'that', the 'li' is an element of distance, and the ending '-kum' tells you the speaker is addressing a plural 'you' — it specifies the audience, not the thing pointed at. It does not change for case.

49.meaning: A noun meaning 'the judgment, ruling, decree, or wisdom' — an authoritative decision or command, and by extension the sound wisdom behind it. It denotes the verdict that settles a matter or the governing rule that decides it.
49.grammar: A verbal noun (the abstract 'act/result of judging'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified (e.g., after 'is'). It signals the word is functioning as a doer or topic rather than an object.

50.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
50.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

51.meaning: He judges / He will judge; He decides, rules, and decrees with authority — passing a binding verdict and governing a matter wisely.
51.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, 'he judges/will judge,' describing a single male subject (or 'He,' of Allah). The ya- prefix marks the third-person masculine singular ('he'), and the final -u marks the indicative mood — an actual, ongoing, or future action.
51.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, rule; wisdom and governance

52.meaning: Between you / among you; the space or relation linking the members of a group.
52.grammar: An adverb of place ('between/among') with an attached pronoun. The fixed -a ending is characteristic of such place-words; the ending -kum means 'you' for a group, so the whole means 'among you all'.
52.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation/interval; the space between two things

53.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
53.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
53.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

54.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
54.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

55.meaning: All-Wise: possessing perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right place with flawless knowledge, judgment, and purpose. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's consummate wisdom.
55.grammar: A masculine singular adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, settled quality of wisdom. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative — the case used for a subject or, very often, a predicate describing the doer ('[He is] All-Wise').
55.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, to be wise

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'it escaped you / slipped past you / got away from you (plural)' — said of something that eludes one or is missed and lost.
2.grammar: A perfect (past) verb, third-person masculine singular ('it/he'). The -a after the stem marks the 3rd-person masculine past form; the long vowel in the middle comes from the weak root. The attached -kum is the object 'you all' (the ones something escaped from).
2.root: ف-و-ت (f-w-t) — to escape, slip away, elude, be missed

3.meaning: A thing, something, anything — an indefinite term for any item, matter, or entity, however small. In negations it yields the sense 'nothing at all'.
3.grammar: The final -un (an 'n'-sound called nunation) marks the noun as indefinite — 'a thing / some thing' rather than 'the thing' — and the -u within it is the nominative case, typically the subject form.

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: Means "your spouses / mates / pairs" — a plural of "spouse or pair," referring to partners (husbands or wives), belonging to a plural "you."
5.grammar: A plural noun in the genitive case (the -i before the pronoun), signalling possession or that it follows a preposition. The attached -kum means "your" (plural). The whole means "your spouses/mates."
5.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — to pair, couple, join; spouse, mate, one of a pair

6.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
6.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

7.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth. The plural form (kuffār) stresses persistent, often defiant denial; the root sense is 'to cover/conceal,' hence to deny what is true and be ungrateful.
7.grammar: A definite plural noun (intensive pattern fuʿʿāl) with the article al- ('the'). The final -i is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of the disbelievers') or follows a preposition.
7.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to disbelieve, be ungrateful

8.meaning: So you took your turn — a verb of reciprocity: when the turn of advantage passes to you and you act in response, requiting or following up on what was done before.

parts.en: took a turn / requited (Form III: acting in response to another)
you (plural) — subject of the past tense

8.grammar: A completed-action (past tense) verb. The fa- prefix means 'so/then', linking it as a consequence of something prior. The -tum ending marks the doer as 'you (a group)': whenever a past verb ends in -tum, it means 'you all did it'. The long ā after the first root letter signals Form III, the pattern of mutual or responsive action — acting toward someone in return.
8.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow behind, come after; hence a turn, a consequence, requital

9.meaning: Then give — a command to hand over or deliver something to someone, from the verb ātā, 'to give, to bring to'.

parts.en: give (command stem, Form IV 'cause to come to = give')

9.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. fa- 'then/so' ties the command to what precedes it as a result. The -ū ending marks the command as addressed to a group: 'you all, give!' Since commands in Arabic are always addressed to 'you', this -ū can only mean a plural addressed group — here it turns the bare stem into an order directed at many people at once.
9.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; in Form IV, to bring/give

10.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
10.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

11.meaning: She (or it, feminine) went away, departed, passed on — the basic verb of going or leaving.
11.grammar: A completed-action (past tense) verb. The -at ending is the standard marker of a feminine singular subject in the past: 'she did' or 'it (a feminine noun) did'. So the form as a whole means 'she/it went'.
11.root: ذ-ه-ب (dh-h-b) — to go, go away, depart

12.meaning: Their spouses/wives — the plural of zawj, which means one member of a pair, hence a spouse or mate.

parts.en: spouses/wives (plural of zawj, 'one of a pair')

12.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessor. The -u- ending before the pronoun is the nominative case, the case of the subject or doer of a sentence. The suffix -hum means 'their', referring back to a group of males (or a mixed group): 'the spouses OF them'.
12.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — to pair, join in a couple; spouse, mate

13.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'like,' 'similar to,' 'the equal of,' or 'a counterpart.' It expresses likeness or correspondence between things.
13.grammar: A noun in the accusative ending -a. This ending typically marks it as the object of a verb, as an adverbial 'in like manner,' or as the first term of a possessive link ('the like of …'). It conveys resemblance or equivalence to whatever it is paired with.

14.meaning: A word meaning 'what' or 'that which' — a relative/indefinite particle pointing to an unspecified thing ('what', 'whatever', 'that which').
14.grammar: An invariable particle (mā) with no case ending. Depending on context it works as a relative pronoun ('that which') introducing a clause, or as an interrogative/indefinite ('what'). It does not inflect for case, gender, or number.

15.meaning: 'They spent / disbursed' — the act of laying out wealth, giving it away, or expending it, done by a group in the past.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb in a pattern meaning to spend or expend (especially wealth). The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the silent alif written after it is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.

16.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'guard yourselves / be mindful and on your guard.' The verb conveys taqwā — protecting oneself by being conscious of Allah and shielding oneself from wrongdoing and its consequences.
16.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you (all).' The -ū ending marks the masculine plural addressees ('you all'). The pattern (form VIII, from waqā 'to protect') gives the sense of taking protective care for oneself.
16.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself

17.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
17.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

18.meaning: A relative pronoun, masculine singular, meaning 'who / which / the one that.' It links a following clause to a noun, marking it out as 'the [noun] that…'
18.grammar: A masculine-singular relative pronoun. It is indeclinable (its form does not change for case) and introduces a description, equivalent to 'the one who/which…'

19.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
19.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

20.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
20.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

21.meaning: Believers: those who have faith — people who inwardly trust and outwardly affirm Allah and what He has revealed. The active participle describes ones characterized by īmān (secure, committed belief).
21.grammar: A masculine plural active participle ('ones who believe'). The suffix -ūna (written wāw + nūn) is a single unit marking the masculine sound plural in the nominative case: it names a group performing or characterized by the action and is the form used when the word is the doer or topic of a sentence.
21.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust, to have faith

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: The Prophet — a person to whom Allah sends revelation and a divinely guided message for humankind. The word denotes one who conveys tidings from Allah, or (on another derivation) one of high and exalted rank.
2.grammar: A definite singular noun marked by the prefixed 'al-' ('the'). The doubling (shadda) on the nūn is not part of the base word: it results from the 'l' of 'al-' assimilating into the following 'n' (a 'sun letter'), so 'al-nabiyy' is pronounced 'an-nabiyy'. The base noun is نَبِيّ (nabiyy). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or the one being described.
2.root: Two derivations are held by grammarians: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings, weighty information (one who brings tidings); or ن-ب-و (n-b-w) — to be high or elevated (one of exalted rank), favoured by those who note the doubled yāʾ pointing to an original wāw.

3.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

4.meaning: It came to you / reached you — a completed arrival of something reaching a person (one male).
4.grammar: A past-tense verb, 'he/it came', whose final -a vowel is the inherent third-person masculine singular inflection built into the verb form itself (not a separate piece). The attached pronoun -ka ('you', one male) is the object reached — 'it came to you'.

5.meaning: "The believing women" — the feminine plural of mu'min, one who has īmān: settled faith and trust in Allah that brings inner security.

parts.en: believing (one who has faith; doer-form of Form IV 'to believe')

5.grammar: 'The' plus a feminine sound plural noun. The -āt ending marks a plural of women or feminine things. The final -u is the nominative case ending: it typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence — the one doing or being something ('the believing women come…').

6.meaning: They (women) pledge allegiance to you — from bāyaʿa, literally to strike a mutual bargain (from the vocabulary of buying and selling), used for the solemn hand-pledge of loyalty and obedience.

parts.en: pledge/make a compact (Form III: a two-sided exchange)
they (a group of women) — feminine plural subject

6.grammar: A present-tense verb. The yu-…-na frame marks the subject as 'they (women)': the -na ending is the fixed feminine plural marker and never changes for mood. The long ā of bāyiʿ signals Form III, the pattern of mutual dealing — a pledge is given and accepted on both sides. The final -ka is an attached object pronoun, 'you (masculine singular)'.
6.root: ب-ي-ع (b-y-ʿ) — to sell, transact; Form III: to conclude a pact, pledge allegiance

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
7.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').

8.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
8.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

9.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
9.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

10.meaning: They (women) associate partners — the verb of shirk: setting up anything as a partner or rival alongside Allah in worship or devotion.

parts.en: associate a partner (with Allah) — Form IV stem
they (a group of women) — feminine plural subject

10.grammar: A present-tense verb whose subject is 'they (women)': the yu- prefix plus the -na ending together mark the feminine plural. This -na is invariable — feminine plural verbs keep it regardless of the particles before them. The yu- with a following i-vowel stem marks Form IV, 'to make something a partner', i.e. to ascribe partners to Allah.
10.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, be a partner; Form IV: to ascribe a partner (to Allah)

11.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
11.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
11.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

12.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
12.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

13.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
13.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

14.meaning: They (women) steal — to take another's property secretly and wrongfully.

parts.en: they (a group of women) — feminine plural subject

14.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix plus the -na ending mark the subject as 'they (women)' — the feminine plural. This -na ending is fixed and does not change with mood, so the same form serves in statements and in conditioned clauses alike.
14.root: س-ر-ق (s-r-q) — to steal, take by stealth

15.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
15.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

16.meaning: They (women) commit zinā — unlawful sexual relations, intercourse outside the bond of marriage.

parts.en: they (a group of women) — feminine plural subject

16.grammar: A present-tense verb from a root ending in a weak letter (y). The ya- prefix and the -na ending together mark 'they (women)': the -na is the unchanging feminine plural marker, so the long -ī- before it belongs to the verb stem itself, not to a case or mood ending.
16.root: ز-ن-ي (z-n-y) — to commit unlawful sexual intercourse (zinā)

17.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
17.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

18.meaning: They (women) kill — to take a life, to slay.

parts.en: they (a group of women) — feminine plural subject

18.grammar: A present-tense verb. The frame ya-…-na marks the subject as a group of women: 'they (feminine) kill'. The -na feminine plural ending is invariable — it stays the same whether the verb stands alone or follows particles that would alter other verb forms.

19.meaning: Their (feminine) children / offspring. The plural walad denotes those born to someone — sons and daughters together.
19.grammar: A masculine plural noun ('children') with the possessive pronoun -hunna ('their', referring to a group of females). The -a ending marks the accusative case, typical of a direct object.

20.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
20.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

21.meaning: 'They (females) come to' / 'they commit / perpetrate' — from the verb meaning 'to come', here in the sense of bringing about or committing an act. The subject is a group of females.
21.grammar: A present-tense verb with a feminine-plural subject ('they [women] do/commit'). The -na ending here is the subject marker for a group of females (and is a fixed part of the feminine-plural verb, so the verb's mood does not change this ending). The core sense is 'to come (to)', extended to 'commit/perpetrate' an act.
21.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, bring about

22.meaning: With a buhtān — a stunning slander: a fabricated accusation so outrageous it leaves its victim speechless, from a root meaning to dumbfound.
22.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with'). The -in ending does two jobs: the i-vowel is the genitive case, required after any preposition, and the final n (nunation) marks the noun as indefinite — 'a slander', not 'the slander'.
22.root: ب-ه-ت (b-h-t) — to astonish, dumbfound; hence a slander that stuns

23.meaning: They (women) fabricate it — to invent something falsely out of nothing and attribute it as though real; deliberate forgery of a claim.

parts.en: fabricate/invent falsely (Form VIII of 'to cut', i.e. to cut a lie from whole cloth)
they (a group of women) — feminine plural subject

23.grammar: A present-tense verb with an attached object. The ya-…-na frame marks 'they (women)' — the -na is the fixed feminine plural subject marker. The infixed -ta- after the first root letter signals Form VIII, which here gives the sense of deliberately concocting. The final -hu is the object pronoun 'it'.
23.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — to cut, split; Form VIII: to fabricate a lie

24.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
24.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
24.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

25.meaning: Their (women's) hands — the plural of yad, 'hand', with a feminine plural possessor.
25.grammar: A plural noun plus possessor. The plural aydī ends in a long -ī that absorbs the short case vowels, so the case is not visible on this word — the same written form serves as subject or object. The suffix -hinna means 'their' and refers specifically to a group of females: 'the hands OF them (women)'.
25.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — hand; by extension power, agency

26.meaning: And their (women's) feet — the plural of rijl, 'foot/leg', joined by 'and' and owned by a feminine plural possessor.
26.grammar: wa- 'and' links this noun to a preceding one and makes it share the same case. The -i- before the pronoun is the genitive ending: the case a noun takes after a preposition or when linked as '… OF …' — or, as with wa- here, when it is coupled to another genitive noun. The suffix -hinna is 'their', referring to a group of females.
26.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — foot, leg; also the root of rajul, 'man' (one who goes on foot)

27.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
27.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

28.meaning: They (women) disobey you — to defy or refuse the command of someone owed obedience.

parts.en: they (a group of women) — feminine plural subject

28.grammar: A present-tense verb with an attached object. The ya-…-na frame marks the subject as 'they (women)'; this feminine plural -na never changes for mood. The long -ī- belongs to the weak-final stem, not to an ending. The final -ka is the object pronoun 'you (masculine singular)'.

29.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
29.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

30.meaning: Maʿrūf — literally 'the known/recognized': whatever is acknowledged by sound minds and revelation as right, good, and fitting. The standing Qur'anic term for recognized good conduct.

parts.en: what is known/recognized as right and good

30.grammar: A passive participle — the ma-…-ū- pattern turns the verb 'to know' into 'that which is known/recognized'. The -in ending combines the genitive case i-vowel (the case used after a preposition or in an '… OF …' link) with nunation, the final n that marks the noun as indefinite.
30.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize; hence maʿrūf, what is recognized as good

31.meaning: Then accept their (women's) pledge — a command to one man to conclude the compact of allegiance with a group of women, receiving their solemn pledge of loyalty.

parts.en: accept the pledge / conclude the compact (command, Form III mutual exchange)

31.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. fa- 'then/so' presents the command as the consequence of what precedes. The bare stem bāyiʿ with no personal ending is the command form addressed to one man: 'you (sir), make the pledge-compact'. The long ā marks Form III, the two-sided pattern — a pledge offered and accepted. The suffix -hunna is the object 'them (women)'.
31.root: ب-ي-ع (b-y-ʿ) — to sell, transact; Form III: to conclude a pact, pledge allegiance

32.meaning: A command meaning 'and seek forgiveness' — an appeal to Allah to cover, pardon, and protect one from the consequences of sin. The verb conveys actively asking for that pardon, not merely wishing for it.
32.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'do (you) seek forgiveness.' The form built on the ist- pattern conveys 'to ask/seek for' something, so it means 'request forgiveness.' The bare ending with no final vowel marks it as a direct order. The wa- prefix simply links it to what precedes as 'and.'

33.meaning: 'For them / to them' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a feminine-plural 'them'.
33.grammar: The preposition li- ('for, to') with an attached object pronoun -hunna ('them', feminine plural). It expresses that something belongs to, is owed to, or is on behalf of a group of females. (The vowel appears as 'la-' before the pronoun.)

34.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
34.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

35.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
35.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

36.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
36.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

37.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
37.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.

38.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
38.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: 'You turn away' / 'you turn your backs' — to turn aside, retreat, or shun, often implying rejecting or abandoning something. Addressed to a group.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form V, 'to turn oneself away') addressed to a group of males ('you all'). The 'ta-' prefix marks the second person, and the final '-aw/-ū' element marks the plural subject. The shortened form (without a final 'n') signals the subjunctive/jussive — used after particles like 'if' or 'lest,' giving a sense such as 'if you turn away.'
5.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near; to turn toward or away, take charge

6.meaning: 'A people, a folk, a community' — a group of human beings bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared standing.
6.grammar: An indefinite collective noun. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) marks it as the object of an action.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group, people

7.grammar: A word form; its grammatical role is determined by its position and the case ending.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
9.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
9.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

10.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
10.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

11.meaning: "They despaired / have given up hope" — yaʾisa is to lose hope completely, to cut off expectation of something ever coming.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb. The final -ū is the past-tense plural ending meaning "they (a group of men/people)": the action of despairing is complete and attributed to a group — "they have despaired".

12.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
12.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

13.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
13.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
13.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

14.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
14.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

15.meaning: He despaired / lost hope: to give up hope entirely, to become certain that something hoped for will not come. It conveys hopelessness and resignation.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he/it despaired'). The final -a is the standard close of a past-tense verb in this person, indicating a single masculine subject who completed the action.
15.root: ي-أ-س (y-ʾ-s) — to despair, to lose hope

16.meaning: The disbelievers — kuffār is the intensive plural of kāfir, one who 'covers over' the truth: who knowingly rejects and buries the reality of Allah and His revelation. The root also yields 'ingratitude', since the ungrateful person covers over a favor.

parts.en: disbelievers (emphatic plural of kāfir, 'one who covers the truth')

16.grammar: A definite plural noun. The prefix al- is 'the'; before this word its l assimilates smoothly in recitation. The doubled middle letter (kuffār) is an intensive plural pattern used for classes of people. The final -u is the nominative case: the ending a noun carries when it is the subject or doer of its sentence.
16.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to disbelieve, to be ungrateful

17.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
17.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

18.meaning: Companions, associates, fellows; those who keep company with or belong to a thing — people closely bound to something (often 'people/inhabitants of …').
18.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of ṣāḥib ('companion'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically links the word to a following noun ('companions OF …') or follows a preposition. As a plural it denotes a group, here in a possessive/linking relationship.
18.root: ص-ح-ب (ṣ-ḥ-b) — companionship, to accompany, keep company

19.meaning: The graves — the plural of qabr, a burial place dug in the earth; collectively, the resting places of the dead.
19.grammar: The definite article al- ('the'; its a is swallowed in flowing speech, leaving l-) + a broken plural of the fuʿūl pattern. The final -i is the genitive ending: the case a noun takes after a preposition ('in the graves') or as the second half of an 'of'-phrase ('the people OF the graves').
